The image shows a mango leaf with:
- Whitish-gray powdery patches scattered across the upper leaf surface
- Irregular, dusty/mealy coating concentrated in patches
- No dark necrotic lesions, no dieback of tips, no black sooty layer
- The white powdery deposits are characteristic of fungal sporulation on the surface

This matches **Powdery Mildew** — the hallmark symptom is white-to-gray powdery fungal growth (Oidium mangiferae) on the leaf surface, exactly as seen here. It does not match Sooty Mould (which would be a uniform black coating), Anthracnose (dark necrotic lesions), or Die Back (tip/shoot death).
